subject: QuantumBridge pilot: integration recap, streaming + funcall design, next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Pat Huang <pat@quantumbridge.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantumbridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuantumBridge pilot: integration recap, streaming + funcall design, next steps

Hi Pat / Sanjay —

Thanks again for a great call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. I tried to focus the summary on the integration items that will unblock a small pilot (2-week runtime + eval) you described.

Top pain points you shared
- Live agent transcripts and knowledge-layer reranking are inconsistent in latency and cost; current infra trips at peak loads (~120 concurrent agents).
- Need deterministic structured outputs for downstream billing/workflow systems (JSON schema required).
- Tooling surface: engineering wants an easy path to support streaming and function calling (tool invocation) without a big SDK rewrite.

Goals for the pilot
1) Ingest live transcript stream -> produce incremental structured hypotheses (streaming tokens + partial JSON fills)
2) On finalization, emit embeddings + 1-pass rerank of candidate KB passages (top-5) in <300ms median on your staging load
3) Keep per-message inference cost within the envelope you shared (~$0.02/message target) using batching + KV cache

Integration & product-fit notes (what we discussed)
- SDK changes: minimal client-side patch — our plan is to provide a thin wrapper method (stream_to_structured) that supports chunked streaming and a final commit call. We scoped the patch so it fits under your existing 2.x client.
- Function calling: Redwood will expose a stable funcall contract for "invoke_tool" that maps to your internal action bus; we'll provide typed signatures so your devs can handle success/failure deterministically.
- Streaming: use Redwood streaming + prefix caching; we recommend 200ms micro-batch and a 2s max latency SLO for interactive agent UX.
- Embeddings + rerank: we propose computing embeddings at commit time and running a single rerank pass (dense + lightweight re-score) using our small quantized model to control cost.

Open questions for your team (please confirm):
A) Which schema validator do you want us to align with for structured outputs (JSON Schema v4 vs proto)?
B) Do you have an existing short-lived token exchange flow for routing model calls from your front end to Redwood, or should we help scope an auth proxy?
C) Do you require encryption-in-transit only, or do you need customer-managed keys for embeddings at rest for the pilot?

Proposed next steps
1) We’ll send a short SDK diff + migration notes by Monday (attached patch).
2) Engineering sync (30 min) next Wed to walk through streaming handshake + funcall signatures — propose Nov 18 10:00 AM SGT / 18:00 UTC.
3) Pilot kickoff: Redwood provides 2-week reserved capacity plus runbook; QuantumBridge provides example transcript feed + success metrics.

Attachments: quantumbridge-mvp-integration-diagram.pdf (infra diagram), redwood-sdk-diff.patch (client wrapper), sample-structured-output-spec.yaml

If any of this is off, say so — otherwise I’ll set the calendar and drop the materials.

Thanks,
Sean
SEAN GALLAGHER
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Pat Huang <pat@quantumbridge.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantumbridge.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: QuantumBridge pilot: integration recap, streaming + funcall design, next steps

Thanks Sean — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- For structured outputs we prefer JSON Schema v4 (we already validate messages in our event pipeline).
- We do have a token-exchange flow (short-lived JWTs issued by our auth service) but no reverse proxy yet; we'll want guidance for secure routing from client -> Redwood.
- For the pilot, embeddings at rest should be encrypted by Redwood; customer-managed keys are something we may ask for later but not required for initial POC.

Sanjay and I can make the Wed slot work; please send an invite. Also the infra diagram looks right — will review the SDK diff when you send.

Pat
Product Lead, Integrations
QuantumBridge
pat@quantumbridge.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@quantumbridge.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QuantumBridge pilot: integration recap, streaming + funcall design, next steps

Appreciate the answers, Pat. Two engineering clarifications on our side: 

1) Schema: JSON Schema v4 acknowledged — we’ll produce the sample schema and adapter in the SDK diff so your validators can ingest directly.
2) Auth/proxy: if you already have short-lived JWTs, the lightest integration is to validate tokens in the auth proxy we provide and then mint short-lived model access tokens. Ben will lead the design doc for the proxy.

Marissa — can you confirm we have a small quantized reranker image available in staging for the Nov 18 walk-through?

Ben

Thanks all — this looks good and aligns with our objectives. A couple quick confirmations before the Wed sync:

- We’ll provide a 30-minute sample transcript feed (JSON stream) and a small KB snapshot for rerank testing.
- We confirm JSON Schema v4.
- We’ll be OK with Redwood-managed keys for the POC. For production we’ll want CMKs but we can scope later.

Please send the calendar invite for Nov 18 10:00 SGT. Looking forward to the walk-through.

— Sanjay
